Half-Car CFD simulation

Half-car aero simulation of the Formula Electric car in STAR-CCM+.

Team
UBC Formula Electric, Aerodynamics
Software
STAR-CCM+
Mesh
15 million cells
Result
188 N downforce, 75 N drag

Results

  • 188 N downforce and 75 N drag, about 2.5 to 1
  • Residuals below 10-4
  • Run on the standard fixed-attitude CAD

Setup

  • SolidWorks car geometry imported into STAR-CCM+
  • Half of the car modelled, using symmetry
  • Rectangular domain above a ground plane
  • Trimmed cell mesh with refinement around the wings, wheels and suspension
  • Prism layers at the walls

Next

  • Cornering runs with the dynamic CAD model

Dynamic CAD Model

Adjustable car model in STAR-CCM+, built for cornering simulation.

Team
UBC Formula Electric, Aerodynamics
Timeline
July to August 2026
Software
STAR-CCM+, SolidWorks
Status
Model built, simulation in progress

Why

  • Cornering means yaw, roll, steer and camber
  • A fixed model can only test one attitude

What I built

  • Controls for yaw, pitch, roll and ride height
  • A coordinate system at each wheel, so steer and camber are independent
  • SolidWorks to STAR-CCM+ integration, so it follows the team's CAD

Status

  • Model is built
  • Not yet used in a CFD run
  • Cornering simulation is being set up

Magnetic Levitator

Course project: a circuit, coil and machined parts that hold an object in mid-air.

Type
Course project
School
UBC Mechanical Engineering
Electronics
Soldered through-hole PCB
Machining
Mill, lathe, press brake

How it works

  • Hall effect sensor reads the magnetic field
  • LM324 op-amps and a transistor adjust the coil current
  • The object stays suspended below the coil

Circuit

  • Hand-soldered the control board from the lab schematic
  • Offset and gain trimmers for tuning

Metal parts

  • Made parts on the manual lathe and mill
  • Bent sheet metal on the press brake
  • Worked from the course drawings

Front Wing Design

Three-element front wing designed in SolidWorks for a design competition.

Type
Design competition, personal
Software
SolidWorks
Airfoils
S1223 main, E423 flaps
Envelope
620 by 250 mm

Profile

  • S1223 airfoil for the main element, E423 for the flaps
  • Elements 360, 135 and 90 mm long
  • Angles of 6°, 15° and 32°
  • Fits a 620 by 250 mm envelope
  • Fully dimensioned sketch, so one edit updates the whole wing

Model

  • Profile extruded across the span
  • Endplates added

Small Engine Rebuild

Teardown and rebuild of a 158 cc Briggs and Stratton XR 550 Professional.

Type
Personal project
Timeline
September to December 2022
Engine
Briggs and Stratton XR 550, 158 cc
Tools
Calipers, micrometers, hand and power tools

What I did

  • Fully disassembled the engine and inspected each component
  • Measured the cylinder bore and other critical parts with calipers and micrometers
  • Checked every measurement against manufacturer specs
  • Cleaned, lubricated and reassembled with new gaskets
  • Finished in good running condition
  • Later repaired similar engines in quads and dirt bikes
